diagnostic_evidence.quote: The capacity is right-continuous as a set function, meaning that for compact sets $K_n, K$ with $K_n\downarrow K$, one has $\capacity(K_n)\downarrow\capacity(K)$. Hence, we can compute the capacity of each output set $\Gamma_n^{\spec}(A)$ to obtain a $\Pi_1^A$ algorithm.
Moreover, if the limit in \eqref{limit_well-behaved} is from above or below, then $\{\Xi,\Omega,\mathbb{R},\Lambda\}\in\Pi_1^A$ or $\{\Xi,\Omega,\mathbb{R},\Lambda\}\in\Sigma_1^A$, respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in Sigma_1^A/Pi_1^A requires the level-1 outputs to converge monotonically to Xi. Assumption (S1) only gives Sp(A) subset Gamma_n^spec(A) with max dist(z,Sp(A)) <= E_n -> 0; the covers (gamma_cover1) are not nested, so |Gamma_n^spec(A)|, Cap(Gamma_n^spec(A)) and M_n(A) converge to their limits but need not be monotone in n. The capacity step is an invalid inference: right-continuity of capacity is invoked for nested decreasing compact sets K_n downarrow K, while the covers are not nested, and thm_warm_up's construction Gamma_n = Gamma~_n - 1/n is likewise not monotone.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each output by its running extremum (max_{m<=n} for the from-above claims, min_{m<=n} for the from-below claims), or replace the covers by the nested sequence intersect_{m<=n} Gamma_m^spec(A), whose intersection is Sp(A) and to which the quoted right-continuity of capacity applies; then all stated classifications follow.
issues.overall_effect: The Sigma_1^A/Pi_1^A claims for the Lebesgue measure, capacity and number of connected components (example_leb_meas, example_connected_components, ex:capacity, cor_assumI_lims) and their (S2) counterparts (cor_assumII_extra_lims, SCI_tab) are not established as stated; only the limits themselves are shown to be correct.
issues.title: Monotone convergence of the (S1) algorithms is never established
issues.why_classification: Running extrema (a trick the source already uses for Phi_n) or nesting the covers is a short local fix that preserves every stated classification and guarantee, with no new lemma or construction needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Similarly, we can build $\Pi_2^A$ algorithms for the decision problems

issues.failure_explanation: The source derives the Pi_2^A tower only for Xi_Lm^dec ("A straightforward check shows that this provides a Pi_2^A-tower") and then claims the same for Xi_cc^dec "similarly". But the two problems have opposite quantifier structure: Xi_cc^dec(A)=1 means sup_n M_n(A) < infinity, i.e. 'exists K for all n: M_n <= K', whereas the analogous tower 1_{max_{n<=n_1} M_n < n_2} converges upward (Sigma_2^A), not downward as Pi_2^A requires. No Pi_2^A construction is given, and one is not "similar": it needs a nontrivial dovetailing over divergence moduli (decreasing family V_j = complement of {M: for all k exists m <= h_j(k) with M_m >= k}) that appears nowhere in the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the missing construction: enumerate computable divergence moduli h_j and set Gamma_{n_2,n_1} = 1 - max_{j<=n_2} 1[for all k<=n_1 there is m<=h_j(k) with M_m >= k]; the inner limit decreases in n_2 to 1_{sup_n M_n<infinity}, giving the claimed Pi_2^A (and, after the extra (S2) limit, Pi_3^A). Alternatively state only the Sigma_2^A/Sigma_3^A bounds that the exhibited covers directly yield.
issues.overall_effect: The classification of Xi_cc^dec as Pi_2^A in cor_assumI_lims, its (S2) counterpart Pi_3^A in cor_assumII_extra_lims, and the corresponding row of SCI_tab are unproved as written; the one-sided (Pi-type) verification advertised for this decision problem is not delivered by any construction in the paper.
issues.title: Pi_2^A classification of the decision problem 'is the number of components finite?' is asserted only by a spurious analogy
issues.why_classification: The claims are recoverable, but only via a genuinely new construction (a dovetail over moduli) rather than the stated analogy; the exhibited data yield the opposite monotonicity. This is more than a routine local edit but needs no new global architecture and no result is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \cref{lem:cover1}'s proof shows there exists $M\in\mathbb{N}$ with $\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m}(A)\subset\widetilde{\Gamma}_{n,m+1}(A)$ for all $m\geq M$, independent of $n$.

There is a surprise in \cref{fractal_dim_final}: the SCI of computing the upper box-counting dimension is one lower than what one would obtain by passing to an additional limit through \cref{thm:box_counting}.
Each classification has a corresponding lower bound (e.g., \cref{sec:limit_per_lower}).

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims these are the SCI classifications and that they are sharp (abstract: 'proving algorithmic optimality'; SCI_tab: 'each classification has a corresponding lower bound'). But the source's own device used in fractal_dim_final to keep the upper box-counting dimension at Pi_2^A - the (S2) covers Gamma~_{n,m} = Gamma^spec_{2^n,m} are eventually constant in m, uniformly in n - works verbatim for the min-versions of the towers of thm:box_counting and thm_Haus (with successive minima in m so that the inner limits exist). Inserting Gamma~_{k+1,m} in place of Gamma^spec_{n(k)} and using the factor-3 estimates, which hold uniformly in m (H^d_{j,k}(Sp) <= H^d_{j,k}(Gamma~_{k+1,m}) <= 3H^d_{j,k}(Sp), N_{2^{-k}}(Sp) <= N_{2^{-k}}(Gamma~_{k+1,m}) <= 3N_{2^{-k}}(Sp)), yields height-2 towers converging from below to the lower box-counting dimension and to the Hausdorff dimension, i.e. Sigma_2^A rather than Sigma_3^A. So the extra limit charged to these two quantities is not needed and the stated classifications cannot be sharp.

failure_location.quote: The lower bounds in \cite{colbrook2022computation} for diagonal operators (which satisfy \textbf{\rm\textbf{(S2)}}) show that the classifications we prove in this section are, in general, sharp.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen fractal_dim_final by replacing its two Sigma_3^A conclusions with Sigma_2^A bounds obtained from the towers of thm:box_counting and thm_Haus with the (S2) covers Gamma~_{k+1,m} and running minima in m, then update SCI_tab and the sharpness/'cost of a limit' discussion; or else keep the Sigma_3^A bounds and withdraw the sharpness/optimality claims for those two rows.
issues.overall_effect: Two conclusions of fractactal_dim_final and two rows of SCI_tab (lower box-counting dimension and Hausdorff dimension under (S2)) are non-sharp, and the accompanying claims of optimality/sharpness and the rule that moving from (S1) to (S2) costs one limit fail for these quantities. The algorithms themselves and all (S1) results remain valid.
issues.title: (S2) classifications for lower box-counting and Hausdorff dimension are one level too high, contradicting the claimed sharpness
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained reoptimization of the source's own towers (merging the (S2) limit into the existing second limit) and strictly strengthens the results, so no new proof architecture and no mathematical loss is involved; nevertheless two theorem conclusions, two table rows and the paper's optimality claims must be rewritten, which exceeds a routine local fix.
